items_A_D.description: VERIFIED file:read - admin.py:176-222 defines SettingsRequest.emailVerificationEnabled, persists it via admin_repo.EMAIL_VERIFICATION_KEY (repositories/admin.py:39,210) and echoes it back in GET /admin/settings. VERIFIED grep across apps/api/app/**/*.py: EMAIL_VERIFICATION_KEY / emailVerificationEnabled is referenced ONLY in admin.py and repositories/admin.py -- it is never read by routers/auth.py's register()/login() flow. By contrast the sibling 'signupEnabled' toggle in the SAME settings object IS enforced (auth.py:85-91, signup_enabled() gate checked before registration). An admin can flip 'Email Verification' ON in the admin Settings panel; the DB value changes and the UI reports it as enabled, but no verification email is ever sent and unverified accounts are never blocked -- the control is fully inert. This is exactly the class of silently-inert admin control the finding spec flags (no honest disclosure that toggling this has zero effect). The router's own comment ('email-verification placeholder', line 172) effectively admits this.
items_A_D.proposed_fix: The admin Settings panel's `emailVerificationEnabled` toggle (`admin.py:176-222`, `repositories/admin.py:39,210`) persists to the DB and is echoed back as enabled/disabled, but is NEVER read by the actual registration flow (`routers/auth.py:81 register()`) — unlike its sibling `signupEnabled` toggle in the same settings object, which IS enforced (`auth.py:85-91`). An admin can turn this ON believing new accounts will require email verification; nothing changes. Proposed fix: EITHER (a) wire real enforcement — add an `emailVerified` column to `User` (additive migration), send a verification email on register() when the setting is on, gate login/full-feature-access until verified — OR (b), if out of scope for this launch, remove the toggle from the admin settings API/UI (or clearly label it "not yet enforced") so it cannot silently mislead an operator about account security posture. Minimal-diff option (b) is recommended given no evidence email verification is advertised as live anywhere else in the product.

items_A_D.description: VERIFIED file:read (lines 282-299) - _dispatch_stripe_event() handles checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated/deleted, invoice.payment_failed/paid, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created with real state changes; customer.subscription.trial_will_end is a bare 'pass' ("hook point for a reminder notification; no state change"). Confirmed the platform DOES support live Stripe trials (repositories/billing.py:409-427, _ENTITLED_STATUSES includes 'trialing'), so this is a genuinely unbuilt notification, not a moot no-op. Does not affect billing accuracy/entitlement (trialing status itself is correctly entitled) - only the proactive reminder email/notification is missing. Webhook still acks 200 idempotently (line 299), so Stripe retries are not an issue.
items_A_D.workstream: UNMAPPED (no existing W-B..W-J covers billing notifications; recommend operator backlog / new workstream)
items_A_D.proposed_fix: Stripe webhook handler `_dispatch_stripe_event()` in `billing.py` has a real branch for every subscription/invoice/charge lifecycle event EXCEPT `customer.subscription.trial_will_end`, which is a bare `pass` ("hook point for a reminder notification; no state change"). The platform genuinely supports live Stripe trials (`trialing` is an entitled status, `repositories/billing.py:409-427`), so trial users currently get no proactive "your trial is ending" reminder. Does not affect billing accuracy/entitlement itself. Proposed fix: implement `_handle_trial_will_end(cur, obj)` that looks up the user by `stripeCustomerId`/`stripeSubscriptionId` and enqueues a real reminder email/notification (reusing the existing email-notification infra, e.g. `app.services.gmail_service` or an app-level notification-digest agent) — or, if reminder emails are out of scope for launch, replace the bare `pass` with an explicit comment/log line stating this is an intentionally-deferred no-op so a future reader does not mistake it for an oversight, and confirm no UI anywhere promises trial-ending reminders.
